what: How many of NASA's nine Artemis III regions must stay open: availability on the published landing sites of Wueller et al. 2026, 2027 to 2030
citation: Wueller, L., Berger, L. M., Christopher, H., Sugimoto, K., Thaker, A. D., Carton, L., Jo, W., Lee, S., Pedrelli, R., Sanchez, P., & Kring, D. A. (2026). Assessing Potential Landing Sites With Favorable Illumination and Accessible, Potentially Volatile-Rich Permanently Shadowed Regions Within Artemis Candidate Landing Regions. Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, 131(3), e2025JE009434. https://doi.org/10.1029/2025JE009434 (CC BY 4.0). Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17084058
nasa_quote: End-to-end mission availability analyses demonstrate that individual regions typically provide limited viable opportunities when all constraints are simultaneously satisfied. To support acceptable annual mission availability and increase flexibility in launch timing, more than one landing regions must be maintained for Artemis III specifically.
nasa_source: George, Rubio, Lawrence, Curell, LPSC 2026 abstract, NTRS 20250011660 (data/reference/sources/artemis3_update_lpsc2026.docx)

rule.sun: Sun up (half the disc above the skyline) every hour of the stay
rule.check: 13 touchdown points within 100 m, the coarser grid, the near-field sampling; 2 m mast
rule.fragile: at a touchdown point the Sun's centre within 0.27 deg of the skyline during the stay, or the Earth's at touchdown
rule.open: at least one published site of the region is a clear Yes that is not fragile
rule.greedy: first the region open most often, then each time the region that adds the most times not yet covered

cross_check.what: Longest run of consecutive days with any part of the Sun above the skyline in each midsummer period, 12-hour samples at 00 and 12 UTC, at each published site's centre on our 80 m skyline (2 m), against the paper's SunDaysYY (60 m QuickMap TerrainShadows, 12-hour steps, 2 m)
